schedule: before 7am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Major upgrades never open a PR on their own — they queue on the dependency dashboard until ticked. Keeps a Laravel 13 or Vite 8 bump from landing unannounced.
Laravel first-party runtime packages move as one PR; they are released in lockstep and are pointless to review separately.
PHP dev tooling — not shipped to production, safe to batch.
OpenTelemetry packages have to move together or the SDK and the auto-instrumentation drift apart.
Calendar and billing SDKs stay in their own PRs. A regression in one of these silently breaks sync or billing for every customer, so keep them bisectable and reviewed individually.
The Vite/Tailwind asset pipeline is build-time only and tiny — one grouped PR per week keeps its transitive tree (tar, postcss, rollup) current, which is where the CVE backlog sits.
Flutter/Dart packages batch into one PR; the app ships on its own release cadence.
GitHub Actions batch into one PR.
Docker base images batch into one PR.
The PHP runtime image is tied to composer.json's php constraint and to the extensions installed on top of it. Anything beyond a patch needs a human to change both together.
